In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed system allows to build network emulations in a flexible and efficient way, while maintaining the possibility to use complex simulations.
the synchronization approach presented in this work is able to synchronize the time of the emulated network with the time of the simulation.
the proposed approach is able to synchronize the real-time clock of the real systems with the simulated time of the network simulation and to provide a synchronized network emulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can now build up network emulation setups in which we can use a real system as the network simulator.
we can now emulate a complex simulation with a real system in a synchronized fashion and that we can emulate a real system with a complex simulation in a synchronized fashion.
the simulation is no longer required to be real time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show how to synchronize a network simulation to the real network, even though the simulation is not real-time capable.
the synchronization entity is able to keep track of all the events that are happening in the network and in the real systems and that the virtualization layer allows us to control the real systems.
the synchronization overhead is low, which enables synchronized network emulation to become a practical evaluation method.
